note: Re-judged 2026-11-12 by an independent auditor (author of neither the fix commits nor the new tags and test). RFC 7296 Section 2.4, read in rfc/full/rfc7296.txt: "Since IKE is designed to operate in spite of DoS attacks from the network, an endpoint MUST NOT conclude that the other endpoint has failed based on any routing information (e.g., ICMP messages) or IKE messages that arrive without cryptographic protection (e.g., Notify messages complaining about unknown SPIs)." The {partial} annotation is removed: every SA state in which Ze can receive unauthenticated input now has a tagged unit with a recorded break. Initiator handshake: TestInitiatorAuthSurvivesUnprotectedIKEAuthResponse, TestInitiatorEAPSurvivesUnprotectedIKEAuthResponse, TestInitiatorSecondAuthExchangeCountsUnprotectedResponse (RFC 4739), test/ipsec/ike-auth-corrupt-response.ci, and checkInitiatorSurvivesUnprotectedAuthResponse against strongSwan 6.1.0, all on the openProtected drop-to-error mutant. Responder handshake: TestResponderKeepsOldSAOnUnauthenticatedInit/TestResponderAcceptsReinitAfterStaleSA (IKE_SA_INIT), TestResponderAuthSurvivesUnprotectedIKEAuth, TestResponderEAPSurvivesUnprotectedIKEAuth, TestResponderSecondAuthRoundDropsUnprotectedRequestQuietly. Established SA: TestRteUnownedEstablishedSATrustsNothing (the unowned hand-off arm, cleartext Delete and CREATE_CHILD_SA), TestEstablishedSACountsUnprotectedMessage (owner loop, in window, openProtected mutant), TestEstablishedSACountsUnprotectedOutOfWindowResponse (handwritten mutant in handleOwnedInbound's out-of-window response arm crediting DPD on a drop), TestMobikeRetransmitArmCountsUnprotectedMessage (handwritten mutant in the MOBIKE retransmit arm crediting liveness on a drop). Held reauthentication successor, the former gap: TestHeldSuccessorSurvivesUnprotectedMessage, read in full, drives a checksum-flipped request at the successor's expected Message ID through handleInbound and asserts it stays the pending SA, Established, with the same expected Message ID and cached response, the owned SA and Child SA untouched, no datagram, held-successor-decrypt-failed up by exactly one, and then the genuine probe is answered and cached at its Message ID with the successor still held. Its mutant is openProtected's drop turned into an error, which sends handleHeldSuccessorInbound to respondInnerParseError and dropDeadHeldSuccessor. ICMP: TestRFC7296ICMPUnreachableDoesNotFailTheSA and TestRFC7296ICMPFromThePeerWhileWaitingFailsNothing, with revert records on drainErrorQueue and deliverQueuedError. The transport swallows an unreachable for every SA state, so no state is left out. Positive counterweights, so an ignore-every-error handler fails: TestInitiatorAuthEndsOnAuthenticatedMalformedResponse, TestResponderEAPEndsOnAuthenticatedMalformedRound, and the authenticated Delete subtest that reaches StateDead. Judged not owed: the initiator's IKE_SA_INIT response is unprotected by construction, and Section 2.21.1 says "In an IKE_SA_INIT exchange, any error notification causes the exchange to fail.", so ending that attempt into the ordinary reconnect concludes no peer failure. The out-of-window request arm (inbound.go) returns an empty outcome whatever openProtected answers, so no state change is reachable from it; whether it answers is RFC7296-2.4-12's subject. A message under SPIs no SA holds has no SA to change. Tests not re-run by this judge; records written by another agent, judged from their break text.
